title: Pending Arbitration Does Not Bar a Wilful Defaulter Notice Against a Borrower, Rules Calcutta High Court
case_name: Kitply Industries Limited & Ors. v. Reserve Bank of India & Anr.
card_summary: The Calcutta High Court dismissed Kitply Industries' challenge to a wilful defaulter notice issued by SREI Equipment Finance. It held that pending arbitration over the underlying loan dispute does not bar the lender from pursuing the RBI's wilful defaulter framework, since classification proceedings run on a separate track from the arbitration over the debt itself.
card_tip: Challenging a loan in arbitration does not freeze a lender's wilful defaulter process; a borrower needs a specific order staying that process, not just a pending reference.
verification_notes: Confirmed across Taxscan, SupremeToday.ai and LiveLawBiz; all three agree on the parties, the single judge's holding, and the background NCLT and arbitrator proceedings. Figures for the underlying loan default (Rs 333.58 crore) and the land involved (256 hectares) are consistent across sources but kept out of the short card for space.
